prompt: You are the PM for an AI inbox triage feature. The PRD says: 'Summarise new messages, identify what needs attention, and help users respond faster. The experience should be accurate, helpful, and concise.' Create the smallest eval that can inform a first-release ship decision. There is no production data yet. Make the result usable by engineering.

Design an eval for a travel-booking agent. It can search flights, read traveller policy, place a 10-minute hold, and purchase only after explicit user confirmation. A PM wants to know whether it is safe to dogfood. Include what engineering must record and reset between runs.
watch_for: required, prohibited and conditional tool calls

prompt: Critique this proposed eval for an AI support assistant: 'Collect 30 questions. Ask an LLM judge to score helpfulness from 1-5. Ship if average helpfulness is at least 4.' Explain what could pass while users still fail, then produce a corrected minimum viable version.

A document agent has these five observed failures: cited a paragraph that did not support its claim; edited the wrong file with the same name; asked for confirmation after making the edit; retried a failed write four times; gave a correct final answer despite using a prohibited admin tool. Turn these into a regression set and say what else you would collect. Do not imply five reports are statistically representative.
watch_for: one or more cases per pattern

prompt: A PM has an LLM judge for 'faithful answer'. On 40 human-labelled outputs it agrees 34 times. The six disagreements contain four cases where the judge passed an unsupported claim and two where it failed a supported paraphrase. Advise whether to automate the release gate and define the next calibration step.
watch_for: false passes treated as higher risk

prompt: Write an eval for a CRM clean-up agent. The one-line requirement is: 'Find stale contacts and clean them up automatically.' The agent can merge, archive, and permanently delete contacts. The stakeholder wants something engineering can build this week.
watch_for: does not quietly choose product policy
